scenario_category: several articles describing the same development
description: Two outlets republish the same wire-service text about a regulatory fine; a third outlet adds one genuinely new detail. Tests whether a model treats wire-service reprints as independent confirmation.

event.title: Regulators fine Atlas Retail Holdings over breach-disclosure delay
event.description: Atlas Retail Holdings is fined after a delay in disclosing a customer data breach.

articles.title: Atlas Retail Holdings fined over delayed breach disclosure
articles.summary: Regulator fines Atlas Retail Holdings for delaying disclosure of a data breach affecting customers.
articles.raw_content: Federal regulators have fined Atlas Retail Holdings for failing to promptly disclose a data breach that exposed customer information. The regulator said the company waited several months longer than required before notifying affected customers. Atlas Retail Holdings said it is reviewing its data-handling procedures. The company said millions of customer records may have been affected, though it did not provide an exact figure.

articles.title: Atlas Retail Holdings fined over delayed breach disclosure
articles.summary: Same wire-service report as above, republished under a different outlet name.

The regulator said the company waited several months longer than required before notifying affected customers. Atlas Retail Holdings said it is reviewing its data-handling procedures. articles.title: Atlas Retail Holdings fine set at $4.2 million, filing shows
articles.summary: An original follow-up reporting the specific fine amount, not present in the wire report.
articles.raw_content: A regulatory filing reviewed by Regulatory Watch Daily shows the fine against Atlas Retail Holdings over its delayed breach disclosure was set at $4.2 million. The filing does not specify how many customers were affected. Atlas Retail Holdings has not commented beyond its earlier statement that it is reviewing its data-handling procedures.

must_preserve_facts: Atlas Retail Holdings was fined for delaying disclosure of a data breach
The company said it is reviewing its data-handling procedures
must_not_invent: An exact number of affected customers (only 'millions', not a precise figure, is reported)
Any executive resignation or departure (not reported by any source)
A specific cause of the breach itself (not described — only the disclosure delay is)
known_ambiguities: Articles 11 and 12 are the identical wire-service text republished under two outlet names (same underlying report, not independent corroboration). A good brief's source_references and treatment of corroboration should not be inflated by counting this as two independent confirmations; article 13 is the only genuinely new, independent detail (the fine amount).
validation_notes: Exercises the prompt's rule 4 ('If multiple articles originate from the same wire service or outlet, avoid treating them as separate independent confirmations'). Mechanically, all three article IDs remain valid citation targets — distinguishing real vs. duplicate corroboration here is an editorial judgment call for human review, not something the schema validator can detect.
